blocks.x: NYC’s Village Halloween Parade has revealed its 2026 theme, and it is asking New Yorkers to bring their “Body & Soul” to Sixth Avenue this Halloween.

On Saturday, October 31, the 53rd Annual Village Halloween Parade will once again transform Sixth Avenue into a moving, screaming, dancing gallery of giant puppets, marching bands, performers, and thousands of New Yorkers in costumes that probably took much longer to make than anyone will admit.

The theme announcement arrives just in time for serious costume planners to begin their annual descent into papier-mâché, hot glue, face paint, cardboard engineering, and whatever elaborate group concept has already overtaken the group chat.
Here are more details about the theme and some early parade details ahead of October!

What “Body & Soul” could look like this year
The parade has not issued a costume rulebook for interpreting the 2026 theme, and that is exactly the point.
“Body & Soul” leaves room for the corporeal, the cosmic, the musical, the spiritual, and the completely absurd.

Think anatomical hearts with a disco pulse, skeletons in sequins, giant moving hands, guardian angels, possessed marionettes, human mood rings, jazz-age ghosts, and group costumes that turn “soul” into a full-scale dance party.

None of those are official costume instructions, obviously. They are simply proof that the theme has enough range for New Yorkers to take it in wildly different directions, which has always been the Village Halloween Parade’s real superpower.
How to join the parade
Costumed marchers can join the lineup at Canal Street and Sixth Avenue between 6:30 p. and 9 pm on Halloween night.
The parade begins at 7 pm, and participants are released onto the route in timed groups, so do not expect to simply stroll in at the last second.

The parade’s directions are very clear: only people in costume can march. Organizers recommend meeting friends a block or two away from the route, then arriving together, since the crowd and cell-service chaos can make reunions difficult.
The subway is also strongly recommended because parking in the area is predictably brutal on parade night. Read the parade’s full marcher instructions before heading downtown.

Those who would rather skip the lineup can buy a VIP ticket or join the special theme section, both of which help support the nonprofit arts organization behind the parade. There is also a costume contest, with prizes including tickets to shows and more!

Getty Images / GummyBone
Where to watch
Not marching? Grab a viewing spot somewhere along Sixth Avenue between Canal Street and 15th Street, then prepare to stay put.
The best places get crowded early, especially around Greenwich Village, and the parade’s most elaborate puppets and performers are worth waiting for.

Bring a charged phone, layers, and shoes you can stand in for a while. More importantly, pick a post-parade meet-up location before the crowd scatters, because finding friends after tens of thousands of costumed people pour into Lower Manhattan is about as easy as spotting one specific vampire in a sea of them.
The official parade route, theme information, participation rules, and special-access tickets are available through the Village Halloween Parade website.
The post The world’s largest Halloween parade shutting down NYC’s Sixth Avenue has revealed its 2026 theme appeared first on Secret NYC.
